To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the depressive state is the main factor in suicides with different psychiatric diagnoses.
depressive disorders are a common cause of completed suicides.
depressive manifestations in completed suicides are more severe than in attempted suicides; they are more severe in patients with schizophrenia than in those with affective disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (a) what is the incidence of depressive disorders in suicides; (b) what are the clinical features of depressive disorders in suicidal patients; (c) is there a difference in the features of depressive states in suicidal and non-suicidal patients; and (d) is it possible to predict the development of a suicidal state on the basis of clinical features of the depressive syndrome?
the clinical and nosological aspects of suicide in patients with mental disorders.
the problem of the depressive state in suicide-minded patients with mental disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
depressive states in suicidal patients are a complex phenomenon, which may be associated with various mental disorders.
in suicides with depression the most important factor is the presence of suicidal ideas.
in all nosological groups, depression is a prominent factor, but it is not a sufficient one to explain the suicidal act.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the depressive state in suicidal patients with different nosological diagnoses is not a single nosological entity, and the depressive state of suicidal patients is characterized by the absence of the usual symptoms of depression.
the depressive manifestations in suicidal persons with mental disorders are not uniform.

the incidence of depressive states in suicides is higher in the group of patients with affective disorders, and that the clinical features of depressive states in suicide-minded patients are more severe in the group of suicides with affective disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
depressive manifestations in suicide-minded patients with schizophrenia are different in their clinical picture and in their psychopathology from those in patients with other mental disorders.
the incidence of suicide attempts in patients with depressive disorder is much higher than in patients with other mental illnesses.
the incidence of suicide attempts and completed suicides is highest among patients with affective disorders and lowest among patients with schizophrenia.
